marketMood: Asia leads a quiet July 4 session: a big June jobs miss (+57K), AI-chip profit-taking, and Fed-independence jitters set a cautious but broadly bullish tone heading into H2 2026.

upcomingEvents.event: SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR listing (SKHY) — record ~$29B offering
China Q2 GDP + June retail sales & industrial production
US Section 122 tariffs (10%) expiration deadline — Congress must act

topStories.headline: June Payrolls Miss Badly at +57K; Unemployment Holds at 4.2%
topStories.summary: The US economy added just 57,000 nonfarm jobs in June — well below the ~115K consensus — while April and May were revised down a combined 74,000; unemployment held at 4.2% and labour force participation dipped to 61.5%.
topStories.marketImpact: S&P 500 closed flat on the data; ↓ rate-hike probability (now ~11% for July); ↑ TLT on lower-for-longer bets; leisure/hospitality shed 61K amid World Cup effects

topStories.headline: Trump Renews Push to Reshape Federal Reserve After Supreme Court Blocks Lisa Cook Firing
topStories.summary: Following last Sunday's 5–4 Supreme Court ruling that blocked President Trump from firing Fed Governor Lisa Cook while her case proceeds, the administration is renewing pressure on the Fed's independence and personnel.
topStories.marketImpact: ↓ GLD, TLT — elevated Fed-independence risk premium; markets pricing in potential for a more politicised rate path; watch USD volatility

topStories.headline: Wall Street Enters H2 2026 with Bull Conviction; JPMorgan Lifts S&P 500 Year-End Target to 7,800
topStories.summary: Despite mixed macro data and Middle East headwinds, major banks remain bullish on equities: JPMorgan raised its S&P 500 year-end target from 7,200 to 7,800, citing a 'Blue Sky' AI earnings scenario and resilient consumer spending.
topStories.marketImpact: ↑ SPY — institutional consensus skews bullish; S&P 500 near 7,573; Bank of America flags rising correction risk heading into Q3 as a near-term counterpoint

topStories.headline: Nikkei 225 Falls 2% to ~69,000 as AI Chip Stocks Extend Selloff; Financials and Toyota Buck Trend
topStories.summary: Japan's benchmark index fell 2%, led by steep losses in AI-linked chip stocks: Kioxia (−11.4%), Advantest (−6.7%), Tokyo Electron (−6.2%), Taiyo Yuden (−4.3%); financial stocks MUFG (+1.9%) and Mizuho (+2.4%) and Toyota (+3.6%) outperformed on sector rotation.
topStories.marketImpact: ↓ Japan semis: 8035.T, 6857.T; ↑ Japan financials (8306.T) and autos (7203.T); sector rotation from AI-growth into value accelerating

topStories.headline: Hong Kong Ends H1 as One of World's Worst Performers (−11%); Mainland CSI 300 Up 7.6% on AI Chip Surge
topStories.summary: The Hang Seng Index fell 0.6% to 22,881 today and closed H1 2026 down 11% overall (HSTECH −19%), while mainland China's CSI 300 rose 7.6% driven by domestic AI chip enthusiasm; Cambricon Technologies surpassed a 1 trillion yuan market cap after a 76% YTD gain.
topStories.marketImpact: ↓ HK equities (0700.HK, 9988.HK) — capital flows favouring A-shares over Hong Kong; ↑ mainland China AI/chip names; FXI lagging CSI 300

topStories.headline: Chinese Exporters Rush Shipments Ahead of July 24 US Tariff Expiry; H1 Exports Up ~15% YoY
topStories.summary: With US Section 122 tariffs (10%) expiring July 24, Chinese exporters are accelerating shipments to the US, contributing to a roughly 15% year-on-year export surge in the first half of 2026; June trade and Q2 GDP data follow in mid-July.
topStories.marketImpact: watch — short-term positive for China export-oriented names; FXI cautiously supported; key risk is tariff reinstatement post-July 24

topStories.headline: Global AI/Tech Profit-Taking Deepens; Nvidia Off ~4%, AMD and Qualcomm Down 9%+ at Worst
topStories.summary: A global de-risking trade in AI infrastructure stocks continued this week, with Nvidia tumbling ~4%, AMD and Qualcomm losing over 9% at session lows, and South Korea's Kospi dropping 10% at the peak — driven by doubts over the pace and payoff of AI capital expenditure.
topStories.marketImpact: ↓ NVDA, AMD, QCOM, AVGO — valuation reset underway as investors demand proof over promises; South Korean tech (Samsung, SK Hynix both −12%+) hardest hit in Asia

topStories.headline: US-Iran Peace Deal MOU Nearing Finalisation; Oil Subdued Near Multi-Month Lows
topStories.summary: A US-Iran memorandum of understanding is close to formal signing, with President Trump confirming the Strait of Hormuz will reopen and the US naval blockade lifted once completed; oil has stabilised near multi-month lows with the deal largely priced in.
topStories.marketImpact: ↓ Oil largely already discounted; ↑ Asia oil importers benefit from lower energy costs; ↓ XLE, CVX on lower near-term earnings; Goldman Sachs year-end Brent target at $80

companiesToWatch.name: Toyota Motor
companiesToWatch.reason: Outperforming in a weak Nikkei session (+3.6%) on sector rotation away from semis into autos and financials; lower energy costs from Iran deal also benefit the manufacturer.

companiesToWatch.name: NVIDIA
companiesToWatch.reason: AI infrastructure profit-taking continues; down ~4% as markets question the pace of data-centre spending — watched globally as the bellwether for the AI capex cycle.

companiesToWatch.name: Tokyo Electron
companiesToWatch.reason: Among Japan's hardest-hit semis today (−6.2%); the leading barometer of AI equipment demand sentiment in Asia.

companiesToWatch.name: Chevron
companiesToWatch.reason: US-Iran peace deal normalises Persian Gulf oil flows; near-term earnings headwind as Brent edges toward $70–74 range; Q3 guidance will be key.

companiesToWatch.name: SK Hynix
companiesToWatch.reason: South Korean memory giant under pressure in the AI chip selloff; Kospi shed 10% at the height of recent tech weakness; Nasdaq ADR listing (SKHY) on July 10 adds near-term overhang.
